title: Prevention Is Better Than Cure for AI Societal Risks
text:
Prevention Is Better Than Cure for AI Societal Risks

fDi Intelligence

Karl Mondon/AFP/Getty Images

The following excerpt is from an op-ed published in fDi Intelligence on September 22, 2026, written by Wendy Cutler, Senior Vice President of the Asia Society Policy Institute.The debate on how to shape the most effective policies on artificial intelligence has stepped up a notch after the technology’s leading voices called for a development slowdown to address safety concerns.Security matters are paramount when it comes to AI, landing them at the top of the list of US policy priorities in balancing the risks of such a frontier technology with the economic, educational, health and scientific progress it promises to deliver.But for many in the US, the more immediate risks are tangible effects on their everyday life: unemployment, rising inequality and hitting community resources. The US must get ahead and tackle these in an inclusive way at the outset, avoiding the need to take more drastic steps later down the track.We’ve seen this movie before on trade, where similar warnings were sounded but not taken seriously enough. But while the window for action on trade policy may have closed, on AI, we still have time to get it right.Read the full op-ed here.
